issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) requires calculateTotalPrice(Meal) to return a double (for double precision financial calculations), but the solution implements calculateTotalPrice as returning an int. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected return type and precision and may cause test failures if tests expect a double.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the method signature in SealSaloon to match the specification: declare calculateTotalPrice as static double calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal). Use a double accumulator (e.g., double sum = 0.0) and return a double. Ensure any places calling this method (or tests) expect a double return type.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a method calculateTotalPrice(Meal): double (double precision) but the provided solution implements calculateTotalPrice as returning an int. Although the method name is identical, the contract differs (expected double vs implemented int), which can confuse students mapping the requirement to the implementation and tests that expect double precision.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method contract across artifacts. Either change the solution to declare calculateTotalPrice as returning double (public static double calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal)) and compute the sum in double precision, or update the problem statement and examples to expect an int return type. Prefer updating the solution to return double to match the problem requirement (use double sum and add ingredient prices as double).
